What a purge here can and cannot reach

Shards already placed on other peers are recalled — holder by holder, and reported holder by holder.
{{ remote_note }}
A holder that never answers keeps its shard.
Nothing can reach a disk that is offline. Those holders are kept in the node's recall ledger and retried in the background, and they are reported as unreachable — never as deleted, and never rounded up into an overall "purged".
What it does reach: shards on the peers that answer, the object on the storage node's gateway, the copy in the site's own object store, the node's own shard files for that object, this worker's read cache, the database rows that point at it, and the content hash (blocklisted so the same bytes cannot be re-uploaded).
{# THE LISTING. On the same page as the purge form on purpose: an operator who has to carry a canonical target between two screens is an operator who will eventually carry the wrong one. #}
